choices.B: Settlement of a court case after the reporting period confirming that the entity had a present obligation at the reporting date
choices.C: Destruction of a major production plant by fire
choices.D: Announcement of a major business combination

questions.explanation: PAS 10 and PSA 560 distinguish between adjusting events (Type 1: conditions existing at the reporting date) and non-adjusting events (Type 2: conditions arising after the reporting date). The settlement of litigation confirming a pre-existing obligation at year-end requires adjustment of the financial statements.
questions.solution:
Type 1 (Adjusting): Evidence of condition at balance sheet date (e.g. lawsuit settlement, customer bankruptcy, discovery of fraud).
Type 2 (Non-adjusting): Conditions arising after balance sheet date (e.g. fire casualty, stock decline, dividend declaration).
questions.legalBasis: PAS 10 Events after the Reporting Period; PSA 560 Subsequent Events

questions.subject: AUD
questions.question: Which computer-assisted audit technique (CAAT) involves the auditor processing dummy test transactions containing both valid and invalid conditions through the client's live computerized system?
questions.explanation: The Test Data approach involves inputting a set of dummy transactions (with predetermined results containing valid and erroneous data) into the client's computer system to verify whether programmed controls function effectively.
questions.solution:
Test Data: Auditor's dummy data -> Client's live/test program.
Parallel Simulation: Client's real data -> Auditor's independent simulation program.

questions.subject: AUD
questions.question: Under Philippine Standard on Quality Management 1 (PSQM 1), how often must an audit firm perform the monitoring and evaluation of its system of quality management?
questions.explanation: PSQM 1 requires the individual assigned ultimate responsibility for the firm's system of quality management to evaluate, at least annually, the system of quality management and conclude whether it provides reasonable assurance that its objectives are being achieved.
questions.solution: Evaluation of the firm's system of quality management must be conducted at least annually under PSQM 1.
questions.legalBasis: PSQM 1 Quality Management for Firms that Perform Audits, par. 53

questions.subject: AUD
questions.question: If physical inventory count is conducted at a date other than the balance sheet date, what audit procedures must the auditor perform under PSA 501?

choices.B: Perform audit procedures to obtain evidence about whether changes in inventory between the count date and the reporting date are properly recorded (roll-forward / roll-back testing)
choices.C: Rely solely on management's representation letter
choices.D: Disclaim an opinion on the entire balance sheet

questions.explanation: PSA 501 paragraph 5 requires that when physical inventory counting is conducted at an interim date, the auditor shall perform audit procedures to obtain audit evidence about whether changes in inventory between the count date and the date of the financial statements are properly recorded.
questions.solution: Roll-forward/roll-back procedures test purchases, sales, and internal transfers between the interim count date and the year-end balance sheet date.
questions.legalBasis: PSA 501 Audit Evidence - Specific Considerations for Selected Items, par. 5

questions.subject: AUD
questions.question: Under the Philippine Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants, which of the following is NOT one of the five fundamental principles of professional ethics?
questions.explanation: The five fundamental principles under the Code of Ethics are: (1) Integrity, (2) Objectivity, (3) Professional Competence and Due Care, (4) Confidentiality, and (5) Professional Behavior. Maximum profitability is not a principle.
questions.solution: Fundamental Principles: Integrity, Objectivity, Professional Competence & Due Care, Confidentiality, Professional Behavior.
questions.legalBasis: Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants in the Philippines, Section 110

questions.subject: TAX
questions.topic: Individual Income Tax (8% Option vs Graduated)
questions.question: Under the TRAIN Law (RA 10963), a self-employed individual with gross sales of P2,400,000 and operating expenses of P600,000 signified his intention to be taxed at the 8% income tax rate on gross sales in his 1st Quarter return. What is his total income tax due for the year?
questions.explanation: Under the TRAIN Law, purely self-employed/professionals whose gross sales/receipts do not exceed the P3,000,000 VAT threshold can elect the 8% income tax in lieu of graduated rates and 3% percentage tax. The 8% tax is computed on gross sales/receipts in excess of P250,000. Income tax due = (P2,400,000 - P250,000) * 8% = P2,150,000 * 8% = P172,000.
questions.solution:
1. Gross Sales = P2,400,000.
2. Less: Statutory deduction for self-employed = P250,000.
3. Taxable Base = P2,150,000.
4. Income Tax Due = P2,150,000 * 8% = P172,000.
Note: No percentage tax under Sec. 116 is due.
questions.legalBasis: NIRC Sec. 24(A)(2)(b) as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN Law)

questions.subject: TAX
questions.question: Under the CREATE Act (RA 11534), which domestic corporations qualify for the reduced Regular Corporate Income Tax (RCIT) rate of 20% (instead of the standard 25%)?

choices.A: Domestic corporations with net taxable income not exceeding P5,000,000 and total assets (excluding land on which the business entity's office/plant is situated) not exceeding P100,000,000
choices.B: All domestic corporations regardless of net income or asset size
choices.C: Only listed corporations in the Philippine Stock Exchange
choices.D: Corporations operating inside PEZA zones only

questions.explanation: Section 27(A) of the NIRC, as amended by the CREATE Act (RA 11534), provides a reduced 20% RCIT rate for micro, small, and medium domestic corporations whose taxable net income does not exceed P5,000,000 AND total assets (excluding land) do not exceed P100,000,000. Other domestic corporations pay 25%.
questions.solution: Criteria for 20% RCIT: Net Taxable Income <= P5M AND Total Assets (excluding land) <= P100M.
questions.legalBasis: NIRC Sec. 27(A) as amended by RA 11534 (CREATE Act)

questions.subject: TAX
questions.question: Under the Ease of Paying Taxes (EOPT) Act (Republic Act No. 11976 enacted in 2024), what single commercial document is now the sole substantiation requirement for both sales of goods and sales of services for VAT and income tax purposes?

choices.A: Official Receipt (OR) for both goods and services
choices.B: VAT Sales Invoice (or Commercial Invoice) for both goods and services

questions.explanation: The EOPT Act (RA 11976) unified the invoicing requirements by establishing the Invoice as the sole primary document to substantiate both sales of goods and sales of services for VAT output/input tax and income tax deductibility, eliminating the requirement of Official Receipts for services.
questions.solution: EOPT Act (RA 11976) Reform: 'Invoice' is now the primary document for sales of both goods and services. Output VAT on services is now recognized upon issuance of invoice (accrual basis).
questions.legalBasis: Republic Act No. 11976 (Ease of Paying Taxes Act), Sec. 113

questions.subject: TAX
questions.topic: Capital Gains Tax on Real Property
questions.question: Mr. Cruz sold an idle residential lot in Tagaytay (capital asset) for P4,000,000. The zonal value was P4,500,000 and the assessor's fair market value was P3,800,000. What is the Capital Gains Tax (CGT) due on the sale under the NIRC?
questions.explanation: Under NIRC Section 24(D)(1), capital gains tax on the sale of real property classified as a capital asset is 6% of the gross selling price or fair market value (higher between zonal value and assessor's value), whichever is higher. Higher value is Zonal Value (P4,500,000). CGT = P4,500,000 * 6% = P270,000.
questions.solution:
1. Selling Price = P4,000,000.
2. Fair Market Value (Zonal) = P4,500,000.
3. Tax Base = Higher amount = P4,500,000.
4. CGT = P4,500,000 * 6% = P270,000.
questions.legalBasis: NIRC Sec. 24(D)(1)

questions.subject: TAX
questions.question: A domestic corporation paid P65,000 for the residential rental of its managerial employee. Under the NIRC as amended by TRAIN, what is the Fringe Benefit Tax (FBT) due on this benefit?
questions.explanation: Monetary value of housing leased by employer for managerial employee is 50% of the lease payments: Monetary value = P65,000 * 50% = P32,500. Grossed-up Monetary Value (GUMV) = P32,500 / (1 - 0.35) = P32,500 / 0.65 = P50,000. FBT due = P50,000 * 35% = P17,500.
questions.solution:
1. Monetary Value = P65,000 * 50% = P32,500.
2. Grossed-up Monetary Value = P32,500 / 65% = P50,000.
3. FBT = P50,000 * 35% = P17,500.
questions.legalBasis: NIRC Sec. 33 as amended by RA 10963; RR 11-2018

questions.subject: TAX
questions.question: A Filipino citizen died in 2025 leaving a gross estate of P18,000,000, which includes a family home valued at P12,000,000. Funeral expenses were P300,000. Under the TRAIN Law (RA 10963), what is the allowable total deduction for standard deduction and family home, and the net estate tax due?
questions.explanation: Under TRAIN Law (RA 10963), funeral expenses are NO LONGER deductible. Allowable special deductions: Standard deduction = P5,000,000; Family home = actual value up to max P10,000,000. Total deductions = P5,000,000 + P10,000,000 = P15,000,000. Net taxable estate = Gross estate (P18,000,000) - Deductions (P15,000,000) = P3,000,000. Estate tax rate is flat 6%. Estate tax due = P3,000,000 * 6% = P180,000.
questions.solution:
1. Gross Estate = P18,000,000.
2. Deductions: Standard Deduction (P5,000,000) + Family Home (Max P10,000,000) = P15,000,000.
3. Net Taxable Estate = P18,000,000 - P15,000,000 = P3,000,000.
4. Estate Tax Due = P3,000,000 * 6% = P180,000.
questions.legalBasis: NIRC Sec. 86 as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN Law)

questions.subject: TAX
questions.question: Under Philippine Tax Law, what is the statutory gross sales/receipts threshold for mandatory VAT registration for persons engaged in the sale of goods or services?
questions.explanation: Under Section 109(CC) of the NIRC as amended by the TRAIN Law, the threshold for mandatory VAT registration is annual gross sales or receipts exceeding P3,000,000.
questions.solution: Statutory VAT threshold = P3,000,000. Below threshold -> 3% percentage tax (or 8% gross income tax option for individuals). Above threshold -> 12% Value-Added Tax.
questions.legalBasis: NIRC Sec. 109(1)(CC) as amended by RA 10963

questions.subject: RFBT
questions.question: Under the Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines (RA 11232), which of the following is an authorized single incorporator/stockholder of a One Person Corporation (OPC)?

choices.A: A natural person, trust, or an estate
choices.B: A licensed professional partnership of CPAs
choices.C: A bank or non-bank financial institution

questions.explanation: Section 116 of the Revised Corporation Code (RA 11232) states: 'A One Person Corporation is a corporation with a single stockholder: Provided, That only a natural person, trust, or an estate may form a One Person Corporation.' Banks, non-bank financial institutions, insurance companies, and public utilities are prohibited from organizing as OPCs.
questions.solution:
OPC Formation: Only natural person, trust, or estate.
Prohibited: Banks, quasi-banks, insurance companies, public and publicly-listed entities.
questions.legalBasis: Revised Corporation Code (RA 11232), Section 116

questions.subject: RFBT
questions.question: Under the Revised Corporation Code, in which of the following corporate actions does a dissenting stockholder NOT have an appraisal right?

choices.A: Amendment to the articles of incorporation changing or restricting rights of stockholders
choices.B: Sale, lease, or disposition of all or substantially all corporate property and assets
choices.C: Merger or consolidation with another corporation
choices.D: Declaration of 20% stock dividend approved by 2/3 of outstanding capital stock

questions.explanation: Section 80 of the Revised Corporation Code provides for appraisal right in instances such as: (1) amendment of articles changing/restricting rights of shares or extending/shortening corporate term; (2) sale of all or substantially all assets; (3) merger or consolidation; and (4) investing corporate funds in another business. Declaration of dividends does not give rise to appraisal rights.
questions.solution: Appraisal right instances (Sec. 80): Amendment of rights/term, Sale of all assets, Merger/Consolidation, Investment in secondary purpose.
questions.legalBasis: Revised Corporation Code (RA 11232), Section 80

questions.subject: RFBT
questions.question: Under Article 1484 of the Civil Code (Recto Law) governing installment sales of personal property, if the seller chooses the remedy of foreclosure of the chattel mortgage upon the buyer's default in two or more installments, can the seller recover any deficiency if the foreclosure sale proceeds are insufficient to cover the balance of the debt?

choices.A: Yes, the seller may sue for the deficiency judgment
choices.B: No, the seller shall have no further action against the purchaser to recover any unpaid balance of the price
choices.C: Yes, provided there was an express stipulation in the mortgage contract
choices.D: Yes, but only up to 50% of the deficiency

questions.explanation: Article 1484 (3) of the Civil Code explicitly provides that if the vendor has chosen to foreclose the chattel mortgage on the thing sold, he shall have no further action against the purchaser to recover any unpaid balance of the price, and any agreement to the contrary shall be void.
questions.solution:
Recto Law (Art. 1484) Alternative Remedies:
1. Exact fulfillment (sue for specific performance)
2. Cancel the sale (2 or more defaults)
3. Foreclose chattel mortgage (2 or more defaults) -> Absolute bar to deficiency recovery.
questions.legalBasis: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1484(3)

questions.subject: RFBT
questions.question: Which of the following is a key legal difference between Dacion en Pago (dation in payment) and Cession (payment by cession)?

choices.A: Dacion en pago involves all assets of the debtor, whereas cession involves only a specific property
choices.B: Dacion en pago transfers ownership of a specific property to extinguish an obligation, whereas cession transfers only the possession and authority to sell the debtor's properties to satisfy claims
choices.C: Dacion en pago requires the insolvency of the debtor, whereas cession requires solvency
choices.D: Dacion en pago always involves multiple creditors, whereas cession involves only one

questions.explanation: In Dacion en pago, ownership of a specific property is transferred to the creditor and extinguishes the obligation to the extent of the agreed value. In Cession (Art. 1255), the debtor cedes all properties to multiple creditors, transferring only authority to sell and apply proceeds, generally requiring insolvency.
questions.solution:
Dacion en pago: 1 creditor, specific property, ownership transferred, extinguishes obligation.
Cession: Multiple creditors, all debtor assets, authority to sell only, extinguishes up to net proceeds.
questions.legalBasis: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1245 & 1255

questions.subject: RFBT
questions.question: Under Article 1839 of the Civil Code, what is the correct order of priority in settling liabilities upon partnership liquidation?

choices.A: 1. Outside creditors -> 2. Partner claims other than capital/profits -> 3. Partner capital contributions -> 4. Partner share in profits
choices.B: 1. Partner capital -> 2. Partner profits -> 3. Outside creditors -> 4. Partner loans
choices.C: 1. Outside creditors -> 2. Partner capital -> 3. Partner profits -> 4. Partner loans
choices.D: 1. Inside creditors -> 2. Outside creditors -> 3. Partner capital -> 4. Partner profits

questions.explanation: Article 1839(2) of the Civil Code sets the rank of claims against partnership assets: (1) Creditors other than partners; (2) Partners other than for capital and profits (e.g. loans/advances); (3) Partners in respect of capital; (4) Partners in respect of profits.
questions.solution: Order of Priority: 1. Third-party Creditors -> 2. Partner Loans/Advances -> 3. Partner Capital -> 4. Partner Profits.
questions.legalBasis: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1839(2)

questions.subject: RFBT
questions.question: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA - RA 9160 as amended), what is the threshold amount for a Covered Transaction in cash or other equivalent monetary instrument involving banks and non-bank financial institutions?

choices.A: Exceeding P500,000 within one banking day
choices.B: Exceeding P1,000,000 within one banking day
choices.C: Exceeding P250,000 within one banking day
choices.D: Exceeding P5,000,000 within one banking day

questions.explanation: Under AMLA (RA 9160) Section 3(b), a Covered Transaction for financial institutions is a transaction in cash or other equivalent monetary instrument involving a total amount in excess of Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (P500,000) within one banking day. (Note: for casinos, threshold is > P5,000,000; for real estate dealers, > P7,500,000).
questions.solution:
Covered Transaction Thresholds:
- Banks & Financial Institutions: > P500,000 in 1 banking day.
- Casinos: > P5,000,000.
- Real Estate Dealers: > P7,500,000.
questions.legalBasis: RA 9160 as amended by RA 10365 & RA 11521

questions.subject: RFBT
questions.question: Under the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines (RA 8293), what is the statutory term of protection for a Patent granted for an invention, computed from the filing date of the application?

choices.C: 50 years during lifetime of author plus 50 years after death

questions.explanation: Section 54 of the Intellectual Property Code (RA 8293) provides that the term of a patent shall be twenty (20) years from the filing date of the application, non-renewable.
questions.solution:
Patent for Invention: 20 years from filing date (non-renewable).
Utility Model: 7 years (non-renewable).
Industrial Design: 5 years (renewable for 2 consecutive periods of 5 years each).
Trademark: 10 years (renewable indefinitely).
Copyright: Lifetime of author + 50 years after death.
questions.legalBasis: Intellectual Property Code (RA 8293), Section 54
